newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on correction.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Wednesday on a technical correction after sharp falls on Tuesday, traders said.
The most active March 1997 contract ended at 20,500 yuan ($2,469) per tonne, up 60 yuan. It opened at 20,530 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 20,370 and a high of 20,550.
December rose 240 to 20,370, January 40 to 20,480, February 50 to 20,480, April 60 to 20,480 and May 60 to 20,470 and June fell 160 to 20,510.
Combined volume fell to 81,670 tonnes from 85,620.
Copper opened slightly up but fell before short-covering pushed contracts up from low levels.
Traders said wary investors liquidated their short positions after sharp losses, with the short-term trend unpredictable.

"A technical correction was responsible for today's rises, but the potential for further increases will be limited because most contracts did not breach the 20,500-yuan level today," one traders said.
"The low spot price will also limit the potential for rises," he added. The spot price of copper is about 20,000 yuan per tonne in Shanghai.
"The fact that copper did not breach the key 21,500-yuan resistance level indicated the end of the strong rebound of the past two weeks," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to test the 20,000-yuan level in the next few days on poor market sentiment.
Aluminium ended down. The only traded December contract ended at 13,800 yuan, down 50 yuan, on negligible volume of 20 tonnes, traders said.
